# Hostile / edge input corpus (SPEC-107)

Hand-built edge inputs driven through the native CLI (`tests/hostile_inputs.rs`). Of the 8
files here, only `empty_alpha_obu.avif` is also driven through headless wasm
(`tests/wasm_roundtrip.rs`) — the other four wasm hostile-input cases (zero-byte, non-image
text, truncated JPEG, oversize PNG) use separately generated bytes, not these committed
files (see each fixture's entry below). Distinct from `tests/fixtures/fuzz/`, which is
the *fuzzer-found crash reproducer* corpus with its own provenance rule (one file per
fuzzer finding, DEC-062) — nothing here came from a fuzzer. Every file is generated
deterministically by `tests/hostile_inputs.rs`'s `build_corpus::regenerate_hostile_corpus`
(or, for the AVIF fixture, `src/image/avif.rs`'s `generate_empty_alpha_obu_fixture`) —
regenerate with `cargo test --test hostile_inputs -- --ignored regenerate_hostile_corpus`
and `cargo test --lib generate_empty_alpha_obu_fixture -- --ignored`, and the checked-in
bytes are expected to come out byte-identical. Each file is under 4 KB (AC-1).

- **`zero_byte.png`** (0 B) — an empty file. Not an image at all; exercises the
  "undetectable format" path with the smallest possible input.
- **`text_as.jpg`** / **`text_as.png`** (44 B each) — plain ASCII text saved under image
  extensions. No image header a format guesser could ever match.
- **`truncated.jpg`** (758 B) — a real 96×96 gradient JPEG (`common::gradient_jpeg`), cut
  to 60% of its encoded length. Missing the trailing EOI marker (`FF D9`) but long enough
  that the JPEG decoder still produces a complete frame — the exact shape of F1 (a
  truncated JPEG decodes "successfully" and silently, instead of erroring like PNG/AVIF
  do). Below ~50% the same generator produces a hard decode error instead, which is a
  different (already-covered) failure mode, not F1 — see the code comment for the
  measured boundary on this fixture's content.
- **`truncated.png`** (168 B) — a real 96×96 solid PNG (`common::solid_png`), cut to a
  third of its encoded length: long enough to carry a valid IHDR, short enough to be
  missing IDAT/IEND. Decodes to a typed `unexpected end of file` error (unlike JPEG, PNG
  does not tolerate truncation).
- **`truncated.avif`** (143 B) — the committed `tests/fixtures/avif/solid_16x16.avif`,
  cut to half its length. Decodes to a typed container-parse error.
- **`pixel_count_bomb.png`** (57 B) — a forged PNG header (real CRC32, empty `IDAT`/`IEND`
  so the decoder's header-only peek can complete) declaring 20000×20000 pixels
  (400,000,000 px), well over the 64 Mpix decode budget (DEC-063). Distinct from
  `tests/cli.rs`'s existing 70000×1 per-dimension case (DEC-034) — this is the
  pixel-*count* cap.
- **`empty_alpha_obu.avif`** (317 B) — a conforming AVIF whose alpha item's OBU stream is
  genuinely empty (SPEC-094's crafted-container technique: two `iloc` entries at the same
  `mdat` offset, so the primary item drains the real bytes and the alpha item drains the
  now-empty leftover). Generated by `src/image/avif.rs`'s `build_avif_with_empty_alpha`
  over the real primary OBU from `tests/fixtures/avif/solid_16x16.avif`, and committed so
  the CLI and wasm harnesses drive the SAME artifact the SPEC-094 `debug_abort()` guard is
  pinned against (AC-4) — one source of truth, not two copies that could drift apart.
